_README: The training charter (#5068, epic #5067): the ONE source of every training target the engine, the critics, the coaches and the skills read. HAND-OWNED (deploy/config_ownership_audit.py); any change needs an owner ruling and a change_log entry. This file is PUBLIC. The owner-only twin (body/appearance targets) is never committed — see config/training_charter.private.example.json and lambdas/training/training_charter.py. Published surfaces read ONLY training_charter.public_view() (the PUBLISHED_WHITELIST); the target date and the rate band are not on it (owner ruling 2026-10-18: no May countdown or May target on the site). ADR-164.

change_log.by: owner rulings 2026-10-18 (the elite-panel training review, #5067)
change_log.what: First charter: the frame, the rate band, the 5-day split, the step floor and target, the cardio menu, no scheduled deload, effort ceilings, rotation cadence, gated movements, the concession ledger.
change_log.rule: any change needs an owner ruling; bump `version` and add a line here

change_log.what: Added `progression`: the gain rule (two top-of-range exposures at or under the effort ceiling earn one 5-lb step, reps back to the bottom) and the self-raised-load rule (a load the owner raised himself at or under the ceiling becomes the next floor and is graded progressed, not a breach). The redline copy is retired; the engine reads it here.

The level table, the prep doses and the spacing rule's sequence reading are platform-chosen within the ruling.

change_log.by: owner direction 2026-10-18 on the nutrition elite-panel review (#5096, epic #5091: the redlines' titration rule gets a reader); weekly refit built on the panel default, pending R1
change_log.what: nutrition.titration: the weekly titration engine's rule (lambdas/health/titration.py), MOVED here from nutrition.calories.titration (same rule values: 150 kcal step, 14-day spacing, never on a week with fewer than 6 complete logs, not before day 21, two consecutive out-of-band reads, steps before food) and nutrition.calories.titration_record. The band it reads is the charter rate band (governing_goal.rate_band_lb_per_wk through training.rate_band, the clinical guidance cap applied) above the landing, and the redlines' own landing schedule step (target to cap) from the landing down: the redlines' old 'target +/- 0.5 lb/wk' band is retired, so one band governs both the rate target and the titration. The step is sized from the miss (500 kcal/day per lb/wk, 3500 kcal per lb over 7 days), rounded to 50 and held inside min_step_kcal..max_step_kcal. owner_redlines energy_floor_kcal.titration reads this block (max_step_kcal is the one step-size key; the old step_kcal duplicate is dropped). Every rule value is required: a missing one holds the week as insufficient_data, never a fallback. trend_days must equal the shared loss-rate window. A complete log is a day at or above the redlines' dark-day line, and the first step waits for the redlines' complete_days_before_first_titration (both read from owner_redlines, not copied). The redlines' owner rule 'walking FIRST, then food, never both inside 14 days' is kept as a walking-first hold; the steps-floor precondition on top of it is the panel interpretation, pending an owner ruling on epic #5091. The modelled `expected_path` moves with the block; `insufficient_loss_with_logging_intact` is carried by the walking_first rule and the redlines tripwire loss_insufficient_adherent.

change_log.by: owner rulings 2026-10-23 (attended, Session CD) on #5091 R1/R2, the walk-first rule and the step size, #5099, #5205, #5212 and #5207; and the three follow-ups the owner ruled the same day on #5091 (PR #5265)
change_log.what: R1 'stay ~1,500 kcal, re-target the charter': nutrition.calories.target_kcal 2100 -> 1500 and prescribed_band_kcal [2000, 2100] -> [1400, 1600] (centred on the target, #5099); the 1,600 any-day, 1,900 lifting-day and 1,800 seven-day-mean floors are KEPT and become warnings (floor_role: the resolver no longer clamps a target up to a floor; a target or a day under one is reported, never hidden). Records written under an earlier charter version are not the base (records_from_version). nutrition.titration.above_ceiling_action 'warn': the weekly engine no longer pushes food up when the loss is faster than the band ceiling; it holds and warns, and the step it names is max_step_kcal. 'Step size: 150 kcal everywhere' (#5205): max_step_kcal 150 is the one step every redline tripwire and critic line states. 'Walk-first rule: keep the steps check': steps_before_food is owner-ruled, no longer pending. R2 'more protein, but keep 16:8': nutrition.eating_window 16:8 and the four feedings fit inside it (protein.fasting_window). 'Lower the carb floor to ~60 g; protein and fat floors stay' (#5212): nutrition.floors.carb.floor_g 120 -> 58, the whole gram the 1,500 kcal base day holds after the protein (170 g) and fat (65 g) floors (1500 - 680 - 585 = 235 kcal = 58.75 g; a 60 g floor would put the base day itself under its own floor). nutrition.training_day: fat is held at the larger of fat_pct_of_base_kcal and the fat floor. Follow-ups (owner ruling 2026-10-23, #5091): (1) '`planned_minimum_any_weight_kcal` 1,700 -> 1,400. It matches the band floor, so the engine can step food down within [1,400-1,600]. The steps-first rule still applies before any food cut': planned_minimum_any_weight_kcal 1700 -> 1400, steps_before_food unchanged. (2) '+150 kcal on lifting days, so lifting days are about 1,650 and rest days about 1,500. The week averages above 1,500 by design. Rest days are not paid back below the target': the rest-day payback is removed (training_day.balance and rest_day_rule; no payback cap, no uplift_grain_kcal); a lifting day is 1,650 kcal = protein 170 g, fat 65 g, carbohydrate 96 g, a rest day 1,500 kcal = 170 / 65 / 59 g; the session carbohydrate is scaled to fit the lifting day: pre_session.carb_g 40 -> 24 and post_session.carb_g 60 -> 36 (60 g of the day's 96 g, leaving 36 g for the food that carries the 35 g fibre floor; 40 + 60 = 100 g exceeded the whole day). (3) 'Food-plan grader: energy rows grade against the 1,500 target. The 1,600/1,800 lines show as warnings, not failures': read by training.food_panel while floor_role is warning (config/panel_rubric.json). records_from_version is 1.21.0 (main's 1.20.0, #5261, predates the re-target).

change_log.what: #5121: early_warning, the relapse early-warning detector's thresholds as data (health.early_warning, run nightly by daily-insight-compute): min_signals 2 (two lapse signals together raise ONE owner-only flag, one alone never does), lookback_days 60 (a channel with no record inside it is absent, never silent), and six signals beside the four the detector already read: weigh_in_cadence (3 days without a weigh-in), food_log_gap (2 of the last 3 days under the titration rule's complete-log line), step_drop (the 7-day mean 35% or more under the 28 days before, n 5 and 14), checkin_silence (3 evenings with no answered check-in after at least one answered), weight_reversal (the 7-day weigh-in mean 1 lb or more above the 7 days before, n 3 each) and sessions_below_plan (under 3 Hevy sessions in each of the last 2 weeks). The flag is owner-only: stored in USER#matthew#SOURCE#early_warning_flag, sent by the response owner (failure_mode.response_owner) on the owner's own Telegram seat, never on a published surface and never in the shared brief context.

governing_goal.mentality: time-bound, must-hit: every expert school is synthesized and each concedes something to the deadline (see concession_ledger)
governing_goal.target_date_role: a milestone that ends phase one, never a finish line: the plan continues past it (phase_after_may, #5130)

rate_band_lb_per_wk.note: always shown in lb AND as a percent of bodyweight

governing_goal.precedence: the owner clinical guidance record (USER#matthew#SOURCE#clinical, GUIDANCE#current) outranks the rate band wherever the two conflict; it is reference context, never a gate on intensity

phase_after_may.frame: toward the long-term goal and maintenance — the frame does not end at the target date
phase_after_may.target_date_is: the end of phase one: a milestone with a plan after it, never a finish line (#5130)
phase_after_may.rule: the charter is re-versioned on an owner ruling before the target date, not after it
phase_after_may.plan_location: phase_after_may.plan in this charter: the owner writes the post-deadline plan (what the months after the target date hold, toward the long-term goal and maintenance) and it lands here on his ruling, as a version bump with a change-log line; null until then

plan_prompt.rule: from weeks_before_target weeks before the target date, while plan is null, the owner channel carries one dated prompt to write the post-deadline plan; from dead_man_weeks_before_target weeks before it, still null, the row is at the dead-man (the owner-only calibration dead-man alert). The floors are WARNINGS (floor_role): nothing clamps a target up to a floor; a resolved target or a planned day under its floor carries a floor warning, and the critics grade logged days against them, visibly. The lifting-day and any-day floors grade single days; the 7-day-mean floor is reported, not enforced. prescribed_band_kcal is the calorie habit's floor and ceiling, centred on the target (#5099).

titration.read: the shared 14-day least-squares loss rate (mcp.shared_quantities.loss_rate_lb_wk, water weeks excluded), read weekly

titration.max_step_kcal_note: the ONE calorie step (owner ruling 2026-10-23: 150 kcal everywhere, #5205): every redline tripwire and critic line that names a calorie step states this value
titration.above_ceiling_rule: losing faster than the band ceiling (3.5 lb/wk at the charter band) on the confirmed reads: the engine HOLDS the target and records a warning (reason above_ceiling_warning) naming the +max_step_kcal step the owner may choose; it never pushes food up on its own (owner ruling 2026-10-23 R1: stay ~1,500). 'up' is the only other value (the pre-ruling behaviour); anything else holds the week as insufficient_data
titration.step_sizing: the miss (lb/wk outside the band edge) x kcal_per_lb_wk, rounded to step_rounding_kcal, held inside min_step_kcal..max_step_kcal

walking_first.rule: the redlines' owner rule (feet before fork): below the floor with steps at the floor, the first confirmed read is a walking-first hold (the cue is the rule's walking action); food comes down only on a later read at least min_days_between_steps after it, with the run unbroken (never both inside the spacing)

complete_logs.rule: a complete day is one whose logged calories are at or above the redlines' dark-day line (a day under it is dark, not complete); the first step also waits for the redlines' run of complete days before the first titration

titration.insufficient_data: no measured trend, a provisional trend window, no weigh-in, an unreadable band or guidance record, an unreadable rule value, or too few complete logs: the week holds with reason insufficient_data, never a guess

titration.basis: the redlines' titration rule, owner-approved v0.3 (#3753); the weekly refit as owner-ruled 2026-10-23 (#5091 R1: stay ~1,500, ceiling flags are warnings; the steps check kept; one 150 kcal step)

maintenance_weeks._note: Planned maintenance weeks (#5107, epic #5093). The one reader is health.maintenance_week, through the weekly titration decision (health.titration): one decision a week, so the charter band and a maintenance week never both rule a date.
maintenance_weeks.dates_rule: a window's own start and end (YYYY-MM-DD, both set) are its dates; while they are null the named travel.windows entry's start and end are (one place for the trip's dates). A window with no dates either way is INERT: listed as unscheduled, it changes nothing. The dates are the owner's to set; today none are set, so the engine is inert until he sets them
maintenance_weeks.target: maintenance: the expenditure reconciliation's best-matching model kcal (health.expenditure_reconciler best_match, the estimate the titration engine already reads), actionable only on a non-provisional loss-rate window; never a number written here
maintenance_weeks.target_rule: the titration record of every ISO week a window touches HOLDS the week's ordinary target (reason maintenance_week; it carries forward unchanged, so the cut resumes at the pre-window number) and lists maintenance_dates and maintenance_kcal; on those dates health.calorie_target.resolve serves maintenance_kcal with the prescribed band moved to it and no lifting uplift (the estimate is the whole day's burn). No actionable estimate: the dates carry the base target with a warning, never a guess
maintenance_weeks.trend_rule: a weekly read whose 14-day trend window holds a maintenance date is not acted on (reason maintenance_in_trend): a week of maintenance food and water would read as a stall
maintenance_weeks.grade_rule: start weight = the latest weigh-in from weigh_in_reach_days before the window's first day up to that day; end weight = the earliest weigh-in in the weigh_in_reach_days after its last day.
